div.head: Nor Grið Line 1
div.ab: [1] 7 on Norðhymbra lage is sanctus Petrus
And on Norðhymbra lage is sanctus Petrus cyricfrið and sanctus Wilfriðus and sanctus lohannes binnan cyricwagum þreo hundred æt cwicum men, and æt dædum botleas.

And according to the law of the Northumbrians, the compensation owed for a violation of Church sanctuary at Saint Peter’s, Saint Wilfrid’s, and within the walls of Saint John’s is three hundred if the victim is alive, but it cannot be compensated for if he is dead.

1. Und im Northumbrer-Recht beträgt [Busse für Verletzung von] Kirchenfrieden des H. Petrus und des H. Wilfrid und des H. Johann innerhalb der Kirchenmauern 3 ‘Hundert’ beim lebend [gebliebenen verletzten] Menschen, und bei getödtetem [ist die That durch Geld] unabbüssbar.

1. And in Northumbrian law [the compensation for breach of] the church-peace of St Peter and of St Wilfrid and of St John within the church walls is 3 ‘hundreds’ for a person [injured but] still living, and for one killed [the deed is] beyond compensation [by money].
div.note: MS G (Cotton Nero A I, f. 96v, after VIII Atr. 5.2, hand c. 1070). Liebermann numbers this text by manuscript line (1–9), as the sheet does; erasure, wear and chemicals have made it partly illegible, and the bracketed letters are his supplements (with readings from G. F. Warner, 1902). Clause 1 runs over lines 1–5. The churches are York Minster, Ripon and Beverley; Wilfrid died 709, John 721; 1 ‘hundred’ of silver = 8 pounds. Liebermann dates the text c. 1015–c. 1050 and compares VIII Atr 1.1, 4 and 4.1. Column K is one line of the MS per row; Liebermann's German and the English are given on the row where each clause begins.
